summary: A mutually confirmed Finder contract now leads to exactly one downstream path, recorded once in finder_downstream_link (unique per contract; a CHECK ties OFFICIAL to a permit and PERSONAL to a personal mating). The row is never updated; cancelling the contract only stamps detached_at. The handoff runs under a per-contract advisory lock plus both animals' locks, so a retry, a double click or both parties at once return the same link. Before linking it re-reads the current records: current owners are the contract parties, both animals are REGISTERED and alive, both have a bound chip, the resolved breed is the same, one is male and one female, and on the official route both have an issued pedigree. OFFICIAL calls the existing startPermit inside the same transaction (its parameter widened from Database to DbClient), so eligibility, pedigree, sex, owner and duplicate-case rules are unchanged. The permit opens at AWAITING_COUNTERPARTY with no permit number and no payment; the counterparty's confirmation, allocation rule, permit fee and association review stay in the permit flow. An open permit the same two owners already started for the same animals is linked instead of duplicated. PERSONAL creates a separate finder_personal_mating with no permit number, review, official allocation or Puppy Card. Legacy personal_declaration records and their one-sided notes are untouched and never feed the last mating. The official date protocol is shared: mating_date_declaration rows belong to exactly one subject (permit_id or personal_mating_id, enforced by num_nonnulls = 1), and dates.ts works on a subject while the permit functions keep their signatures. Either party proposes, only the other confirms that exact version, and a different answer creates an explicit CONFLICTED/PROPOSED pair. A per-subject lock plus a checked conditional supersede makes two racing corrections of one version produce exactly one winner; before this, the supersede result was not checked. Only CONFIRMED rows from both sources feed animal_last_mating, both animals move in the confirming transaction, and the newest date wins regardless of confirmation order. The count grows without naming any partner, and a full rebuild equals the incremental projection. The first confirmed date moves the Finder request to MATING_COMPLETED and releases coordination. On these screens the versioned breed rule (baseline male 14 days, female 6 calendar months) is applied as a warning only. Pregnancy, birth, allocation and Puppy Card remain reachable only from an issued permit, as current rules require; the personal path gets none of them. Two latent defects in shared code were fixed at the root. First, todayCivil returned the UTC day, so from 00:00 to 03:30 Tehran time a mating dated today was refused as a future date; it now returns the Tehran civil day. Second, redactText cut a 10-digit run out of UUIDs in audit payloads; it now sets UUIDs aside before applying its number rules.

limitations: The official permit's own cooldown warning (§17.2, cooldown.* settings) still reads only official permit dates, so a confirmed personal-path date does not warn there. The Finder screens use both sources. Whether personal dates should count on the official side is a product decision (DEC-0222).

A cancelled contract does not cancel an already opened permit. The permit is the association's record, and only its own flow can reject or close it. The link is detached, and the permit stays visible to both owners in the permit list.
Marking a request 'not completed' after a path is chosen does not close that path. A later confirmed date is still recorded but no longer moves the request.
Finder notifications remain in-app only and behind finder.flag.notifications. The date-protocol notifications use the existing mating kinds.
Other code that derives 'today' from toISOString (outside todayCivil) was not audited in this prompt.
prompts/ and prompts-2/ remain deleted in the working tree. This prompt did not delete them, and the deletion is not in this commit.
